judgment.rationale: First SFI: Grade R (rank 0, resolved), Term 2, Skill Area 'EMERGENT READING', Sub-strand 'Emergent reading skills' — 'Uses pictures to ‘read’ simple phrase or caption books'. Second SFI: Grade R (rank 0, resolved), Term 4, Skill Area 'EMERGENT WRITING', Sub-strand 'Emergent Writing:' — 'Draws pictures to convey a message about a personal experience and uses this as a starting point for writing: with help adds a word, phrase or sentence'. The two statements share a genuine, pair-specific conceptual link: the picture–print relationship at word/phrase level, where a drawing carries meaning that is paired with a short piece of text (reading a captioned page on one side; adding a word, phrase or sentence to one's own drawing on the other). That is meaningful complementary reinforcement across the receptive and productive sides of emergent literacy, so the pair is more than generic repetition or broad reusable overlap. It does not, however, support buildsTowards: the endpoints lie in different Skill Areas and Sub-strands, and the Term 4 statement is a different modality and task (supported production with adult help) rather than a deepened, extended, or more independent version of picture-supported caption reading. The nomination signals are weak and largely lexical (token jaccard 0.21 dominated by function words plus 'pictures'/'phrase'; one shared LC tag token 'emergent'; shared Grade R ancestor; weak same-rank proximity), and shared hierarchy, wording, or Learning Components alone cannot establish developmental dependency. Symmetric relatesTo is therefore chosen with null direction; canonical endpoint order is preserved and is not semantic. Evidence limits: both endpoints carry upstream audit/merge context, both have 24 omitted source-evidence items, and the second endpoint's supporting LC evidence is truncated (one LC metadata block aggregates claims from several other SFIs), so this judgment rests on the visible statement texts, Learning Components and resolved hierarchy only.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Grade R Skills (coordinate rank 0, canonical value 'Grade R'), the first in Term 1 / Emergent Reading / 'Emergent reading skills' ('Uses pictures to predict what the story is about: reads pictures and captions showing an understanding that pictures and words are related but different'), the second in Term 4 / Emergent Writing / 'Works with words' ('Identifies a letter or a space between words in print such as their names or familiar words or in a book'). The pair-specific developmental change is a refinement of print concepts: the Term 1 statement establishes the gross distinction that print (words) is separate from and different to pictures, while the Term 4 statement requires finer-grained attention inside the print itself - isolating an individual letter and recognising word-boundary spaces in familiar text. LC evidence supports this shared print-concept strand (shared LC tag tokens 'print', 'awareness', 'emergent'; first SFI's LC tagged 'print awareness', second SFI's LC tagged 'print concepts'), so it is not mere wording repetition: knowing that words are a distinct kind of mark plausibly supports success in segmenting letters and spaces within words. Shared Grade ancestor and weak rank proximity alone were not treated as sufficient; the judgment rests on the statement texts and LC tags. judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade R, Emergent Reading, Sub-strand 'Phonological/Phonemic Awareness' (coordinate rank 0, 'Grade R', resolved for both), the first in Term 2 ('Identifies rhyming words in well known rhymes and songs...') and the second in Term 3 ('Segments oral sentences into individual words using words of one syllable first'). They are complementary oral sound-analysis skills within the same printed sub-strand and both LCs carry the 'phonological awareness' tag, which gives genuine pair-specific instructional coherence rather than mere repeated wording (shared tokens are only the generic 'a' and 'words'). However, neither statement is a substantive extension of the other: rhyme identification in familiar rhymes and dividing a continuous oral sentence into discrete word units address different linguistic units, and no expansion of scope, text length, letter coverage, or independence is evidenced. The nomination signals (shared Grade R ancestor at distance 4, shared LC tag, 'weak' rank-gap-0 proximity, low-Jaccard token/trigram overlap) are hierarchy and wording signals that cannot by themselves license developmental dependency, so canonical symmetric relatesTo with null direction is the complete judgment. Limitations: source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all involved SFIs carry upstream audit/merge context, which is retained rather than resolved.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade R (rank 0) Emergent Reading, but source identity scopes place the first in Term 1 (Sub-strand 'Relates sounds to letters and words': 'Begins to recognise that words are made up of sounds: gives the beginning sound of own name') and the second in Term 4 (Sub-strand 'Phonological/Phonemic Awareness': 'Recognises aurally and visually some initial consonants and vowels especially at the beginning of common words'). This is earlier-to-later within the same grade, which permits first_to_second. The change is substantive rather than mere repetition: the Term 1 statement is emergent, aural, and limited to the single familiar item of the learner's own name, while the Term 4 statement broadens to a range of common words, specifies consonants and vowels, and adds visual (letter) recognition alongside aural recognition. Awareness that words are made of sounds and the ability to isolate an initial sound in one's own name directly supports success in identifying initial consonants/vowels aurally and visually across common words. LC tags ('beginning sound', 'phonological awareness') versus ('initial sounds', 'phonics', 'consonants', 'vowels') corroborate this phonological-to-phonics progression. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated and both carry upstream audit/merge context, but the printed statement texts and term scopes are complete and unambiguous.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade 2 (rank 2), Term 3, under the 'Reading and Phonics' Skill Area, in different printed sub-strands: 'Daily Phonic Activities of 15 minutes' (recognises the first sound (onset) and last syllable (rime) in more complex patterns such as dr-eam, cr-eam, scr-eam, str-eam) and 'Group Guided Reading' (reads aloud from a book at own level in a guided reading group with the teacher, whole group reads the same story). They form a coherent, complementary pair within the same term's reading programme: explicit phonic segmenting/blending work and teacher-guided oral reading of connected text are the analytic and applied components of the same instructional block. That is substantive skill coherence, so this is more than generic repetition. It is not a developmental dependency: the statements are concurrent parallel daily activities in the same Grade and Term with no increase in scope, complexity, independence or text demand from one to the other, and the guided reading is explicitly pitched 'at own level', which is self-levelling rather than contingent on recognising complex consonant-cluster onsets. The nomination signals are weak and non-semantic (shared ancestors, rank gap 0, same source page 97, token jaccard 0.026 on 'in', trigram jaccard 0.008 on 's s') and were not treated as semantic evidence. relatesTo is symmetric with canonical endpoint order preserved and null direction. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all endpoints and ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context, so this judgment rests on the retained statement text and the resolved Grade 2 / Term 3 identity scope.
